source.title: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability

page_placements.theme: IOI components interact through synergy and redundancy

record.tranche_reason: The study uses designed group ablations and held-out subset-intervention prediction on GPT-2-small IOI. These are different from the original circuit-discovery and faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation, but directly test conditional group effects and their predictive value.
record.gate_note: Rows cover only the GPT-2-small IOI experiments. The study does not test the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. HMM, planted-system, Tracr, and Qwen results concern other subjects or tasks; cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study reuses the documented IOI head groups in GPT-2-small (primary P, backup B and negative E Name Movers). It measures group-ablation interactions on the IO−S logit margin. The positive P×B interaction (removing backups hurts more once primaries are gone) directly tests conditional backup (V2). Its repetition across four lexical frames and ABBA/BABA orders bears on V6. It does not evaluate the 26-head circuit, faithfulness, completeness or minimality (V1), any other model (V3), or alternative circuit-finding methods (V4). Its interaction and predictive-model results do not measure how faithful or complete the circuit looks (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that on GPT-2-small IOI their measurements reproduce conditional backup (positive P×B interaction). The Name Mover–Negative Name Mover interaction is the largest and most stable of three tested group-level terms, both in direct ablations (all 8 frame/order conditions, both ablation conventions) and in held-out subset prediction. They state that the method does not discover the IOI groups and that the pair terms are not a complete circuit decomposition (a three-way residual remains). They assign no dominant individual head pair, and the predictive comparison is limited to one template and mean ablation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses designed group ablations and held-out subset-mask prediction to measure finite effects and interactions, rather than discovering and evaluating the original full circuit against faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Direct interaction sizes differ between template-conditioned mean and zero ablation, though their ordering is unchanged. Direct group-ablation interactions and held-out predictive gains also differ in importance: P×B is clear in the group-ablation corner but yields a smaller predictive gain than P×E across the tested masks. The predictive comparison is limited to one prompt template and mean ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the Negative Name Movers raises the IO−S margin (Δ(E)=−2.270 mean, −2.335 zero). That gain nearly vanishes once primaries are removed, giving a P×E interaction of 1.830/1.681. This is the largest held-out predictive term (MAE 0.386→0.259).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Negative Name Movers in GPT-2-small IOI act conditionally on primary Name Mover output (copy suppression), producing the dominant pairwise group interaction.

fits_no_version.finding: Group-pair interactions leave a positive three-way residual (0.319 mean, 0.601 zero ablation). An additive group model predicts held-out subset ablations with R² 0.752, rising to 0.907 with the three pair terms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of the IOI head groups under subset ablation are substantially non-additive, including higher-order interactions.

fits_no_version.finding: Interaction magnitudes change between mean and zero ablation (e.g. Δ(P+E) −0.136 vs −0.769; P×E−P×B contrast 0.750 vs 0.413), though the ordering is preserved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sizes of IOI group effects depend on the ablation convention while their ranking is stable.

record.problems: The IOI study uses group-level rather than individual head-pair interactions. The direct tests cover four lexical frames and two name orders, while held-out prediction uses one template and mean ablation. A three-way residual remains, and the experiment does not test the complete claimed circuit or its original faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria.
record.rows_left_out: No IOI results were left out. The study's HMM, planted-system, Tracr, and Qwen experiments concern other subjects or tasks and are not rows for these IOI circuit versions.

untested.parts: All of it: the 26-head, 7-class circuit, and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality. Only three documented groups (P, B, E) are ablated.
Activation- or attention-level evidence that individual backup heads take over the name-mover role. Only group-level margin interactions are measured.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and tasks (the Qwen experiment is on refusal, not IOI).
No alternative circuit-discovery method is applied to IOI.
No faithfulness or completeness score for the circuit under different ablations, metrics or distributions.
More than two names, and prompt formats outside the four lexical frames. The predictive study uses one template.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked nearly all rows to V1 and V5, but nothing here tests the circuit's faithfulness, completeness or minimality, or how those depend on evaluation choices. Those links are removed, and V1 and V5 are treated as untested; the reader's V1 and V5 limits_scope labels are dropped. The V6 limits_scope label on R8–R15 is dropped: the one-template restriction of the predictive study is an untested part, not a qualifying result. The paper is a methods paper ('mechanistic tomography'); its HMM, planted, Tracr and Qwen experiments are irrelevant to IOI. Preprint; code released.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines three previously documented head groups and group-level effects, not all 26 heads or 7 classes; it does not test the original faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria, or knock out everything outside the claimed circuit.

Tests conditional effects of the Backup Name Mover group under group ablation and subset masks, but does not directly measure individual backup heads taking over computation or their activation-level response.
No IOI circuit comparison across GPT-2 models, sizes, checkpoints, or other tasks.

Does not apply alternative circuit-finding methods or test whether they recover the same circuit. It does compare two ablation conventions and direct versus held-out predictive interaction measurements, covered by V5.

Tests selected prompt and ablation choices and compares direct group interactions with held-out subset prediction. Does not assess the full circuit's explanatory share of ordinary IOI behavior or broadly vary all metrics and ablation methods.

Tests four lexical frames and ABBA/BABA name orders for the direct group-interaction ordering. Does not test more than two names; held-out subset prediction is limited to one prompt template and mean ablation.
